title: Concepts of Social Stratification
text:
Social stratification refers to the structured categorization of individuals into divisions based on socioeconomic factors such as wealth, occupation, and education. These systems create hierarchical layers within a society, meaning that some groups inherently possess greater power and resources than others. The persistence of these inequalities is often maintained through cultural beliefs and institutional structures.

Theoretical approaches vary in explaining the origins and maintenance of class structure. Functionalist perspectives argue that stratification is inevitable and necessary to motivate people to perform specialized roles beneficial to societal stability, suggesting a natural reward system for talent. Conversely, conflict theory posits that stratification is fundamentally rooted in power dynamics, where dominant groups utilize ideology and law to justify their exclusive control over resources.

The relationship between social class and mobility remains a critical area of study. While some societies exhibit high levels of fluid movement between strata (meritocracy), many others display rigid structures, making upward mobility difficult for those born into lower socioeconomic positions. Analyzing these barriers requires consideration of inherited capital—both economic and cultural.
